newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo banks must find ways to service debt-c.banker.
newsitem.headline: Yugo banks must find ways to service debt-c.banker.

text.p: Yugoslavia's banks will solve no problems by extracting debts from their balances, Belgrade daily Nasa Borba quoted a central bank governor as saying.

"Taking out all debts from bank's balances will not solve their problems. Instead, one must seek ways to service those debts," the paper quoted the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic as saying.
"This cannot be done from the budget nor with NBY intervention, but from the state's assets or from its future gross domestic product," Banovic said.
The NBY Vice-Governor insisted that in their restructuring attempts banks first needed to improve and activate their balances, 90 percent of which were blocked.
He also urged banks to abandon their currently dominanant credit activity and turn more to securities.
The second stage in banks' restructuring programme will be to strengthen them financially and the third to improve their management and supervison.
"It is impossible for a bank to go bankrupt without a director or any other member of the management holding any responsibility for it," Banovic was quoted as saying.

The final stage in bank restructuring programme is for the NBY to strengthen its control over the banking system and apply measures to support all those changes, Banovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
